selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Graceful BGP shutdown (RFC 8326): controlled route drain before peer session closure
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: RFC8326 gshut community is advertised by an initiating FortiGate; receiving peer matches that community and lowers local preference on the learned paths before the initiating peer closes or soft-resets the BGP session.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure receiver community and drain preference -> initiate graceful or graceful-soft shutdown -> advertise gshut-marked routes -> receiver changes path preference -> wait configured delay -> close session or restore preference -> verify alternate path and route withdrawal.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Peer does not recognize the community; drain preference is not lower than alternate paths; no alternate path exists; BFD tears the session down before the graceful drain window.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: BGP summary shows In gshut; route lookup shows gshut community and reduced localpref; alternate route becomes best before session closes; after delay peer session moves Idle(In gshut) for graceful mode.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Configure the same gshut community on both ends, choose a preference below the backup path, confirm alternate route installation, use a deliberate delay, and evaluate BFD timers separately before maintenance.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Determine whether a planned maintenance drain is working by correlating gshut community, local preference, alternate best path, and session closure timing.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Initiator and receiver BGP peers with a second route source; community-tagged path is de-preferenced before session closure; alternate path becomes active.
selected_candidates.semantic_uniqueness: No substantially equivalent mechanism was found for this product in the 30-day published-report inventory.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Import password-type objects from FortiGate devices with private data encryption

selected_candidates.failure_class: Imported object exists but password value is missing or replaced; operator confuses blank-with-preserve with empty password; duplicate ADOM object causes secret mismatch; import is mistaken for proof that the managed device's credential changed.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Import wizard explicitly lists password-type objects and prompts; ADOM object references are intact; install preview shows the intended object delta; target FortiGate retains the existing password when the blank-preserve path is selected.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Inventory password-bearing objects before import, answer each prompt deliberately, use blank only to retain the current device password, review duplicate object resolution and install preview, then verify the managed device after installation.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Choose the safe import action when a password-type object already exists in the ADOM and the goal is to preserve the live FortiGate credential.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiData SIEM Xlog ingestion and incident-event handling
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 recognizes FortiData devices and ingests their SIEM Xlog records into the SIEM database; Issue, Risk Record and Integration Event are distinct supported log types with different default event-handler behavior.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Add FortiData device in Device Manager -> receive Xlog files -> inspect Log Browse -> insert records into siemdb/All logs -> default Ingested External Alerts handler evaluates Issue records -> Event Monitor alert; custom handlers are required for other supported record types.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Device is registered but Xlogs do not arrive; raw files arrive but database insertion is stalled; logs are present but no alert appears because only Issue logs are covered by the predefined handler.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Log Browse proves raw Xlog receipt; All logs proves SIEM database insertion; Event Monitor alert proves event-handler processing; absence of an alert for Risk Record or Integration Event does not prove ingestion failure.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Separate transport, raw-file receipt, SIEM database insertion and event-handler evaluation; confirm the FortiData device is added, inspect Log Browse and All logs, then create custom event handlers for non-Issue types.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish an ingestion failure from an expected no-alert outcome when a FortiData Risk Record is visible in Log Browse but not in Event Monitor.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Zero-touch management: auto-topology, auto-network, MSTP and ICL behavior
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch zero-touch defaults combine VLAN 1 native access, DHCP on management/internal interfaces, auto-topology, FortiLink auto-discovery and FortiLAN Cloud; topology detection selects L2 MSTP/native-VLAN behavior or L3 static ICL behavior.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Factory boot -> obtain DHCP parameters -> advertise/discover controller and neighbors -> detect L2 or L3 topology -> apply MSTP instances 0/15 and native VLAN 4094 for L2 or create static ICL for L3 -> form ISL/management topology.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Unintended auto-ISL or topology formation; dual DHCP default gateways create ECMP and steer management/FortiLink incorrectly; operator mistakes a discovery indicator for an active ISL.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Blue auto-network icon indicates active ISL trunk in FortiSwitchOS 8.0; topology view and LLDP neighbors reveal adjacency; DHCP/default-route state explains management path selection; MSTP instances/native VLAN reveal L2 auto-topology behavior.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Design the management/internal DHCP gateway roles, disable default gateway on the interface not used for management when both use DHCP, disable auto-topology only when required by the design, and validate the actual ISL and MSTP state.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Identify why a newly booted FortiSwitch creates unexpected L2 topology or loses FortiLink reachability when both management and internal DHCP interfaces install default routes.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiAP wired-uplink 802.1X supplicant and EAP method negotiation
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A FortiAP can act as an 802.1X supplicant on its wired LAN/uplink, using EAP-FAST PAC-less, EAP-TLS or EAP-PEAP to authenticate the AP itself to the access switch before normal FortiAP traffic is admitted.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAP profile supplies uplink credentials/method -> AP sends EAPOL to switch -> switch relays RADIUS to authentication server -> EAP exchange completes -> switch authorizes port -> CAPWAP/controller traffic can pass -> AP joins controller.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Uplink port remains unauthorized; EAP method mismatch; missing/incorrect client certificate or trust chain; AP authentication succeeds but CAPWAP/controller reachability is still broken.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: `cw_diag -c wan1x` reports selected EAP method, certificate references and Port Status Authorized; switch/RADIUS logs prove the EAP exchange; controller join status is a separate downstream test.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable wan-port-auth in the FortiAP profile, match the switch/RADIUS EAP method, install CA/client certificate material for EAP-TLS, verify Authorized status, then independently test CAPWAP reachability and controller discovery.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Separate wired-uplink 802.1X authorization from wireless client authentication when a FortiAP is powered but never joins its FortiGate controller.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP uplink supplicant -> access switch 802.1X authenticator -> RADIUS server -> authorized switch port -> CAPWAP path -> FortiGate controller.

selected_candidates.remediation_path: Keep endpoint and device-management planes separate, provide IPv4 management addresses for Inventory discovery, validate IPv6 portal/agent routing independently, and document supported L3 polling device families.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: TEAP two-phase local RADIUS authentication with TLS 1.3 and PAC handling
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: TEAP establishes a TLS-protected outer tunnel, then performs inner EAP authentication and authorization; FortiNAC-F local RADIUS supports TEAP with EAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-TLS inner methods, user/computer identity choices, TLS service configuration and PAC opaque-key protection.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client EAP identity exchange -> TLS handshake and server certificate validation -> protected TEAP tunnel -> primary inner EAP method -> optional secondary inner EAP method -> RADIUS policy decision -> network access policy/VLAN authorization.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Outer TLS certificate/EKU or protocol mismatch; inner EAP method or AD/Winbind failure; PAC opaque key mismatch affecting resumption; successful EAP exchange but wrong network access policy or VLAN.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Client TEAP profile and trusted root; RADIUS logs show outer TLS and inner method progression; local RADIUS server config lists TEAP and TLS 1.3; endpoint receives expected production VLAN only after policy authorization.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use a server certificate with required EKU, enable TEAP on the intended local virtual server, configure TLS 1.2/1.3 and inner EAP method, ensure Winbind/AD dependencies, align PAC opaque key when PAC provisioning is used, then validate policy/VLAN separately.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Locate the failing TEAP phase when TLS tunnel establishment succeeds but the inner user/computer authentication does not complete.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Supplicant -> outer TEAP TLS tunnel -> inner EAP-MSCHAPv2/EAP-TLS -> FortiNAC-F local RADIUS/Winbind -> network access policy -> VLAN.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: RADSec client-certificate validation and RADIUS accounting over TLS
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 adds RADSec accounting support and validates each RADSec client's TLS certificate against configured Local or Trusted CAs before passing decrypted RADIUS authentication/accounting requests to the RADIUS daemon.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: RADSec client opens TLS to FAC default port 2083 or configured port -> FAC presents RADSec server certificate -> client presents certificate -> FAC validates chain against Local/Trusted CA -> decrypt RADIUS payload -> RADIUS daemon handles Access/Accounting semantics.
selected_candidates.failure_class: TLS server certificate missing/wrong; client certificate not issued by configured CA; RADSec service not enabled on interface/port; client supports authentication but not accounting/CoA over RADSec; concurrency limit reached.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: TLS handshake and client certificate chain succeed; RADSec connection is established; RADIUS daemon receives decrypted Access/Accounting messages; supported client count and configured port match deployment.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Assign a dedicated RADSec server certificate, import/trust the issuing client CA, enable RADSec on the listening interface/service, verify client certificate subject/chain and port, and confirm the RADIUS client supports the required accounting/CoA message types.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish a TLS client-certificate rejection from a RADIUS policy rejection when the RADSec TCP/TLS connection begins but no accounting request reaches the RADIUS daemon.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: RADSec client certificate -> TLS handshake and CA validation at FortiAuthenticator -> decrypted RADIUS Access/Accounting -> RADIUS daemon.
